title: Gluten-Free Almond Snowflake Cupcakes
shortDescription: Almond flour cupcakes with a soft crumb, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake, dusted like fresh snow with powdered sugar.
description: These gluten-free almond cupcakes use almond flour for a soft, moist crumb with a light nutty taste. I dust them with powdered sugar right before serving for a snowflake look that fits any holiday table.
ingredients: 1/4 cup sliced almonds, toasted, for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F. Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners.
Whisk almond flour, gluten-free flour blend, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, beat butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Mix in almond extract and vanilla extract.
Add the flour mix and milk in three additions, starting and ending with the flour mix. Stir just until combined.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean and tops spring back when touched.
Cool cupcakes in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully.
Once fully cool, dust generously with powdered sugar and top with toasted almond slices.
tips: Use blanched almond flour, not almond meal. Almond meal makes a grainier, denser cupcake.
Dust the powdered sugar right before serving. It melts into the crumb if you add it too early.
Toast the sliced almonds in a dry pan for 3 minutes for extra crunch and flavor.
Store unfrosted cupcakes in an airtight container for up to 3 days, then dust with sugar just before serving.

faq.question: Can I make these dairy-free too?
faq.answer: Yes. Swap the butter for a plant-based baking stick and use unsweetened almond milk instead of whole milk. The crumb stays soft either way.

faq.question: Why did my almond flour cupcakes turn out dense?
faq.answer: This usually means the flour was packed too tight when measured, or the batter was overmixed. Spoon almond flour into the cup and level it, then mix just until combined.

faq.question: How do I keep the powdered sugar snow look overnight?
faq.answer: Powdered sugar absorbs moisture and fades by morning. Dust cupcakes no more than 1 hour before serving for the cleanest snowflake finish.

faq.question: Can I freeze these cupcakes?
faq.answer: Yes, freeze the unfrosted cupcakes in a sealed container for up to 2 months. Thaw at room temperature, then dust with powdered sugar before serving.

conclusion: These almond snowflake cupcakes bring holiday charm without any gluten. The powdered sugar dusting takes seconds but makes every batch look ready for a winter party.
